target.title: feat(workboard): expose dispatch --max-starts to raise the per-pass start cap
target.body:
Closes #100169

## What Problem This Solves

Workboard dispatch intentionally starts at most three workers per pass, but operators with larger queues had no supported way to raise that cap. The existing internal `maxStarts` dispatcher option was not exposed by the CLI or Gateway RPC.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds `openclaw workboard dispatch --max-starts <count>` as a per-pass override. The default call still uses `workboard.cards.dispatch`; capped calls use the additive `workboard.cards.dispatchWithOptions` method so an older Gateway fails before starting workers instead of silently ignoring the requested cap. Input is a strict positive integer, existing write/admin authorization remains unchanged, and starts stay sequential with the existing one-card-per-owner guard.

The cap is request-scoped. No new config or environment surface. No parallel-start semantic change.

## User Impact

Operators can deliberately start more than three eligible Workboard workers in one dispatch pass. Existing commands keep the current default of three. After upgrading, restart the Gateway before using `--max-starts`.

## Evidence

- Added CLI coverage for method selection, forwarding, strict validation, and mixed-version no-fallback behavior.
- Added Gateway coverage for the cap, invalid inputs, legacy-method rejection, method registration, and existing authorization behavior.
- Updated `docs/cli/workboard.md` with the flag, default, mixed-version behavior, and retained owner cap.
- `oxfmt` on touched TypeScript and `git diff --check`: pass.
- Fresh pre-commit autoreview: clean after fixing an unknown-method prefix fallback finding.
- [Exact-head CI run 29245089940](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29245089940): Workboard plugin contracts, production types, and test types passed. target.title: Fix LINE webhook retryable acknowledgement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

LINE webhook handlers acknowledged signed event requests before knowing whether local dispatch even started. If the handler rejected immediately, OpenClaw still returned 200, so LINE would not redeliver a retryable webhook even though the event was not accepted.

The same early-ACK shape existed in the standalone Express middleware, the Node webhook handler, and the shared multi-account monitor route.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change introduces a bounded dispatch-acceptance step for LINE webhooks. Each entrypoint starts event handling, waits one event-loop turn to surface startup-time rejection as a 500 response, then acknowledges with 200 once dispatch is accepted. If processing continues asynchronously, later failures are still logged in the background instead of holding the provider HTTP response for the full agent turn.

The LINE message adapter now defaults to `after_agent_dispatch` while preserving shipped `after_receive_record` support. The exported Node/Express handlers and shared monitor route have a real `after_receive_record` path for compatibility, and unsupported policy inputs normalize to the default dispatch-acceptance behavior instead of hanging.

## User Impact

Immediate LINE webhook dispatch failures can now trigger provider redelivery instead of being swallowed behind a 200 response. Normal successful turns still ACK quickly after local dispatch starts, avoiding long webhook waits while the agent run continues. Existing consumers that inspect or choose `after_receive_record` remain compatible.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts` (60 tests passed)
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/line/src/bot-handlers.test.ts` (28 tests passed)
- Local HTTP transcript through `createLineNodeWebhookHandler`:
  - slow dispatch: `status=200`, body `{"status":"ok"}`, response returned before the pending handler was released
  - immediate dispatch failure: `status=500`, body `{"error":"Internal server error"}`
- `git diff --check -- extensions/line/src/webhook-ack.ts extensions/line/src/webhook.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.ts extensions/line/src/outbound.ts extensions/line/src/webhook-node.test.ts extensions/line/src/channel.sendPayload.test.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.ts extensions/line/src/monitor.lifecycle.test.ts docs/channels/line.md`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` (clean after preserving `after_receive_record` support and narrowing/normalizing the exposed ACK policy)

Remote Testbox proof was not run from this checkout because the local Crabbox wrapper selected binary `0.18.0`, while `blacksmith-testbox` requires Crabbox `>=0.22.0`.

target.title: fix(macos): defer cookie import banner until inline browser opens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS app users could see the browser cookie-import banner while the embedded dashboard was still showing its Gateway connection or authentication screen. The automatic offer previously ran after app launch and every Gateway connection, before the inline browser was used.

## Why This Change Was Made

The first automatic cookie-import offer is now armed only when the inline browser sidebar opens. If that open happens before onboarding or while using a remote Gateway, the request stays pending and runs when an open sidebar first becomes eligible for Local mode. Later sidebar opens do not request it again after the first eligible local attempt. Settings -> General -> Browser login -> Import remains the explicit re-offer path.

This is the narrow timing follow-up to the inline banner introduced in #104591. AI-assisted; reviewed with the repository autoreview helper.

## User Impact

The Gateway connection/authentication screen stays clear. Eligible local-Gateway users see the cookie-import offer when it becomes relevant: during the first eligible inline-browser session.

target.title: fix(doctor): bound AGENTS.md and root-memory file reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`shouldSuggestMemorySystem` and `migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile` in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` read `AGENTS.md`, `MEMORY.md`, and archived `memory.md` with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile(..., "utf-8")`. A malicious or runaway workspace file could OOM the doctor repair path before any diagnosis or merge.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `AGENTS.md` is only scanned for a memory-system reference, so a 1 MiB cap is plenty.
- Root memory files are markdown journals; 8 MiB is generous while preventing runaway files from OOMing migration.
- Existing `catch` behavior is preserved: an oversized/unreadable `AGENTS.md` is treated as missing guidance, and an oversized memory pair is archived but not merged.

## User Impact

- `openclaw doctor` workspace memory checks no longer buffer arbitrarily large files.
- Oversized `AGENTS.md` / memory files are handled gracefully instead of crashing.
- Normal workspace doctor flows work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls with `readRegularFile` capped reads in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts` covering an oversized `AGENTS.md` and an oversized legacy memory file.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/doctor-workspace.test.ts --run
  # 5 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a standalone Node script at `/tmp/proof-101448.mjs` that imports the real helpers from `src/commands/doctor-workspace.ts` and exercises both the normal and oversized paths in isolated temp workspaces:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101448.mjs
=== OpenClaw PR 101448 real behavior proof ===

Normal AGENTS.md -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = false
  (expected false because AGENTS.md references MEMORY.md)

Oversized AGENTS.md (2 MiB) -> shouldSuggestMemorySystem = true
  (expected true: oversized file is treated as missing guidance)

Normal split-brain root memory -> migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile:
  changed: true
  mergedLegacy: true
  archiveOnly: false
  (expected changed=true, mergedLegacy=true, archiveOnly=false)

Oversized legacy memory.md (9 MiB) -> migrateLegacyRootMemoryFile:
  changed: true
  mergedLegacy: false
  archiveOnly: true
  archivedLegacyPath: /tmp/proof-101448-VTwxDZ/.openclaw-repair/root-memory/2026-07-07T10-29-48-239Z/memory.md
  (expected changed=true, mergedLegacy=false, archiveOnly=true)
```

Interpretation:

- Normal inputs continue to work: a workspace with a conventional `AGENTS.md` referencing `MEMORY.md` is recognized as already having memory guidance, and a normal split-brain `MEMORY.md`/`memory.md` pair is merged.
- Oversized inputs are rejected before any downstream processing: a 2 MiB `AGENTS.md` exceeds the 1 MiB cap and is treated as missing guidance, and a 9 MiB legacy `memory.md` exceeds the 8 MiB cap so the legacy file is archived but its content is not merged into `MEMORY.md` (`archiveOnly: true`).

target.title: fix(acp): preserve structured exec approval metadata
target.body:
## Summary

- Back ACP structured exec approval metadata with the real Gateway request contract and public `exec` caller.
- Preserve the originating approval title and `toolCallId` across Gateway-host, Node-host, pending approval, broadcast, and ACP `request_permission` boundaries.
- Correlate structured approvals by `sessionKey + toolCallId` when multiple ACP prompts share one session key.
- Rebase onto current `main`, preserve current abort handling, and keep generated Swift optional initializer parameters source-compatible with default `nil` values.
- **Fix classification:** Root-cause fix at the public exec approval contract and ACP correlation invariant.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — the final rebased HEAD crossed the real Gateway, live-model, ACP permission, and command-completion boundaries; the focused regression, formatting, protocol generation, and diff checks passed.
- **Patch quality notes:** The 19-file diff is the smallest complete canonical chain because caller, schema, pending record, broadcast, parser, translator, generated protocol model, and their focused tests must agree; splitting it would recreate a parser-only or producer-only contract. The test-only `.catch(reject)` surfaces asynchronous harness failures rather than swallowing production errors. The translator's `return undefined` is the intentional ambiguity guard: duplicate matches must not bind an approval to the wrong prompt. A related open PR scan found no competing same-contract or canonical PR for this metadata and correlation gap.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The original parser read `request.title` and `request.toolCallId`, but the canonical producer path could not emit them because public `exec` callers omitted the metadata and the closed Gateway request schema did not accept, store, or broadcast it. After that contract was connected, structured `exec.approval.requested` events still lacked `runId`; with two active ACP prompts sharing one `sessionKey`, the translator used session-only uniqueness and dropped an event even when `toolCallId` uniquely identified the pending tool call.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The change repairs both source-of-truth invariants instead of masking a missing permission request downstream: metadata now originates at the real public exec caller and survives the Gateway contract, while the translator selects the active pending prompt by the correlation identifier already carried by that contract. Unmatched or duplicate ids still fail closed and retain the existing unique-session behavior.

## User Impact

- **Why it matters / User impact:** ACP clients can display the intended exec approval title and correlate the permission request with the original tool call instead of falling back to synthetic values. Concurrent ACP prompts sharing a Gateway session no longer lose an early structured approval solely because session-only matching is ambiguous.

Approval decisions, allowed options, command hydration, and fallback behavior for events without metadata remain unchanged.

## Origin / follow-up

- Follows #79337, which introduced ACP exec approval permission relay support.
- #3257 is related approval visibility context, but this focused Gateway-to-ACP contract fix does not claim to close it.
- No open competing PR was found for this structured exec approval metadata and correlation gap.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** A real public `exec` tool call must carry its display title and tool-call correlation id through `exec.approval.requested` into ACP `session/request_permission`. If two ACP prompts share a session key, a structured event with a matching `toolCallId` must reach the correct ACP session instead of being dropped as ambiguous.
- **Canonical reachability path:** User/model exec input → public exec tool `execute(toolCallId, args)` → Gateway/Node host approval registration → `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` validation and normalization → pending approval request → `exec.approval.requested` WebSocket event → ACP event parser → active pending tool-call lookup → ACP `session/request_permission` effect.
- **Boundary crossed:** Public exec caller to authenticated Gateway approval request and broadcast, then the production ACP stdio bridge to the ACP SDK client's permission callback and final command completion.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** N/A for provider numeric normalization. The change reuses the existing exec display-detail resolver, Gateway display sanitizer, approval record builder, and permission relay option mapping; no new provider-owned range or parallel normalization helper is introduced.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Linux OpenClaw worktree at HEAD `59985b5f0da9f3c3fc131cf71459169e83ad2c26`, Node 22, isolated OpenClaw state and config, a running Gateway on `ws://127.0.0.1:19137`, the configured live model, the production ACP command implementation launched from the current TypeScript source entry, and an official ACP SDK client.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
1. Start the final PR HEAD Gateway with isolated home, state, config, token, and port 19137.
2. Start the ACP stdio bridge from the same HEAD and connect an official ACP SDK client.
3. Create two ACP sessions mapped to the same sessionKey and issue both prompts concurrently.
4. Let the live model invoke exec, answer request_permission with allow-once, and observe the correlated command complete.
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Final-HEAD concurrent same-session correlation
  HEAD: 59985b5f0da9f3c3fc131cf71459169e83ad2c26
  shared sessionKey: agent:main:acp-concurrent-proof-96719488-817e-4369-89e3-27e79e0c1ca1
  pending ACP sessions:
    a873a0ea-970a-45d6-908c-31d0d13c5a76
    e3ec4026-2813-4be6-b4a9-c6d27c94220f
  permission sessionId: a873a0ea-970a-45d6-908c-31d0d13c5a76
  permission toolCallId: call_0d0229bba971421f80ead9f8
  permission title: print text · `printf ACP_CONCURRENT_FIRST_e0b1abab-8663-4ddb-b818-c94e52e4b9dc`
  selected option: allow-once
  command exitCode: 0
  command output: ACP_CONCURRENT_FIRST_e0b1abab-8663-4ddb-b818-c94e52e4b9dc
```

- **Observed result after fix:** With two active ACP prompts sharing one Gateway session key, the real structured approval reached the session whose pending tool call matched `toolCallId`; the ACP client selected allow-once and the matching command completed with exit code 0 and the expected output.
- **What was not tested:** Linked issue #3257 includes a Discord/channel scenario, but this PR does not change that channel path. No third-party ACP GUI, hosted channel, Discord account flow, cross-platform client, or remote CI completion is claimed. A full final-HEAD typecheck/lint/test matrix was not rerun locally; targeted regression, formatting, protocol generation, diff integrity, and the real Gateway/live-model/ACP/exec boundary were verified.

The final capture and tamper-evident receipt are retained as `runtime-acp-concurrent-proof-final.json` and `runtime-acp-concurrent-proof-final.json.live-proof-receipt.json` in the daily-fix evidence directory.

## Implementation Details

- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The public exec caller is the metadata origin; the Gateway schema and pending approval record are the wire-contract source of truth; the ACP translator consumes that event and only binds a unique active `sessionKey + toolCallId` match. No downstream synthetic metadata or parallel approval store is added.
- `ExecApprovalRequestParamsSchema` accepts optional `title` and `toolCallId`.
- The public exec tool forwards its real `execute(toolCallId, ...)` id and resolves the display title only on approval paths.
- Gateway-host and Node-host approval registration pass both fields into `exec.approval.request`.
- The Gateway normalizes both fields, sanitizes `title` with the existing exec approval display sanitizer, stores them on the pending record, and broadcasts that record through `exec.approval.requested`.
- ACP uses the event metadata for `request_permission`, retaining existing fallbacks when it is absent.
- For structured events without `runId`, the translator first requires a unique active pending tool-call match within the same session key; if none exists, it retains the prior unique-session fallback.
- The generated Swift model includes both optional fields with default `nil` initializer arguments, matching current generated-model compatibility conventions.

## Fresh Verification

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts \
  -t "binds structured approvals by tool call id when prompts share a session key"

Test Files: 2 passed
Tests: 2 passed, 26 skipped
```

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check <19 changed TypeScript/Swift files>

All changed files use the expected format.
```

```text
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen.ts
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen-swift.ts
git diff --exit-code -- dist/protocol.schema.json \
  apps/shared/OpenClawKit/Sources/OpenClawProtocol/GatewayModels.swift

Protocol and generated Swift outputs are stable.
```

```text
git diff --check origin/main...HEAD

Exit code: 0
```

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** Rebased through the daily-fix sync path onto current `origin/main`, resolved the generated Swift protocol and exec tool conflicts, preserved current-main abort handling, and removed local conflict state.
- **RF-002:** Fresh review found a concrete repair target that the earlier bot assessment missed: structured events were not using `toolCallId` to disambiguate multiple pending ACP prompts. The translator and regression coverage now address that path, with real ACP runtime evidence.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/acp/translator.permission-relay.test.ts` locks the concurrent correlation invariant; Gateway producer, public exec caller, host registration, parser, and e2e coverage live in the other seven focused approval test files listed above.
- **Scenario locked in:** Two ACP prompts share one Gateway `sessionKey`; a tool-start registers `tool-second` for the second prompt; a structured approval without `runId` but with that `toolCallId` must request permission from the second ACP session, while the same event without a correlation id must not bind ambiguously.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** A translator-only assertion would not prove the metadata is producible, so focused tests cover the caller-to-event contract and one real Gateway e2e test; the concurrent translator test isolates only the newly discovered ambiguity invariant without changing unrelated session scheduling.
- Gateway schema and producer coverage for optional metadata and display sanitization.
- Public exec caller and Gateway/Node host forwarding coverage.
- ACP parser and translator coverage, including multiple prompts sharing a session key.
- Running local Gateway e2e coverage with a separate approval observer.
- Fresh test types, lint, bundled protocol tests, protocol generation check, formatting, and diff checks.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:availability`, `merge-risk:compatibility`, and `merge-risk:security-boundary` because the diff touches the public Gateway schema, approval delivery, generated protocol models, and permission correlation.
- **Risk explanation:** Availability risk is limited to approval delivery selection; compatibility risk comes from optional wire fields and generated clients; security-boundary risk comes from correlating an approval with a pending prompt. The 19-file diff is broad by file count because it carries one optional contract through all canonical boundaries and focused tests, not because it adds unrelated behavior.
- **Why acceptable:** Both fields are optional and preserve existing fallbacks. Correlation requires a unique active match within the same session key; duplicate or unknown ids fail closed rather than forcing a binding. Titles use the existing display sanitizer, approval decisions and command policy are unchanged, protocol generation is stable, and real Gateway/ACP behavior plus focused regression coverage exercised the affected seams.

## What Was Not Changed

- **What did NOT change:** ACP permission option mapping, Gateway approval decision policy, command hydration through `exec.approval.get`, legacy agent approval event parsing, provider contracts, and unrelated channel delivery remain unchanged.
- ACP permission option mapping or Gateway approval decision policy.

- Legacy agent approval event parsing.

target.title: test(extensions): derive Firecrawl batch expectations from tracked tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `scripts/test-extension.mjs` tests hard-coded the Firecrawl extension as having exactly two tracked test files. That made the tooling test brittle: when Firecrawl gains or removes tests, the batch-plan assertions and exact-exclude coverage can go stale independently of the extension test planner's real inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `listTrackedTestFilesForRoots()` helper to derive Firecrawl's tracked test files from the same inventory source as the extension test planner. The assertions now verify the planner output against the current tracked Firecrawl tests instead of a manually maintained pair of filenames.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. This only makes the extension test tooling coverage track Firecrawl's actual test inventory, so future Firecrawl test additions do not silently leave the batch exclude assertions under-covered.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12d74a8b5298d2b9b078d1c9615fc256e2298cfe`

Validation:

- Focused test: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> 1 file, 44 tests passed.
- Format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> passed.
- Lint: `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` -> passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` -> clean.
- Types: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` -> passed.
- Autoreview: `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` -> passed with no findings.

Scope note:

This PR previously included Firecrawl inherited-config hardening. That was removed after review because normal authored JSON/JSON5 config and include merge paths do not preserve a prototype-bearing Firecrawl config object, and the production hunk overlaps the broader own-property config PR in #103492. The current head changes only `test/scripts/test-extension.test.ts` and does not change Firecrawl runtime config semantics.
